question.text: How many of the top 2026 AI labs will reference animal welfare in their models' guidelines at the end of 2034?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the number of companies from the following list that, as of December 31, 2034, explicitly state in their LLM fine-tuning instructions that animal welfare is a consideration: Alibaba, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, OpenAI, xAI.

If different instructions are used for different models from the same company, then the corresponding company will be counted if at least one set of currently used instructions mentions animal welfare.
question.fine_print:
For the purposes of this question, "fine-tuning instructions" include any document or guidelines that are either directly used in the training of the LLM (e.g., [Anthropic's Constitution](https://www.anthropic.com/research/constitutional-ai-harmlessness-from-ai-feedback)) or provided to human raters whose output is used to train the LLM (e.g., OpenAI's [ModelSpec](https://model-spec.openai.com/)).

*Given the Animal Futures Tournament timeframe, scores from this question will not be included in the tournament leaderboard. However participants are required to predict on at least two of the three long-term questions, as per the tournament rules.*

research:
Two companies already appear to qualify: Anthropic clearly, and OpenAI probably. That is up from one in the question's May 2026 background. I found no animal-welfare language from Alibaba, DeepSeek, Google, Meta or xAI, but my searches for their guidelines were thin, so treat that as "not found" rather than "confirmed absent."

## 1. Resolution source
No single source decides this. Resolution depends on each company's published fine-tuning documents.
- Undated page (current version published 2026-01-21/22): Claude's Constitution lists "Welfare of animals and of all sentient beings" among the values Claude weighs. It also names harms to "non-human beings" as costs. I read only the first half of the page. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/constitution); [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/21/anthropic-revises-claudes-constitution-and-hints-at-chatbot-consciousness)
- 2026-10-29: OpenAI's latest Model Spec is the version dated 2026-10-29. In the first 100k of 123k characters I found no animal-welfare text, only incidental animal mentions. My attempt to read the remainder failed with a tool error. [Model Spec](https://model-spec.openai.com/2026-10-29.html)

## 2. Current status
- Anthropic qualifies today.
- OpenAI very likely qualifies since 2026-10-29, based on secondary sources:
  - 2026-10-30: one commentary says the new spec lists "Effects on other people, animals, or the environment" among side effects. It also describes two new examples where the assistant raises animal welfare, including wild animals, without being asked. It calls these the first positive mentions in any public version; the earlier spec mentioned animals once, negatively. [Sandcastles](https://sandcastlesblog.substack.com/p/openai-model-spec-animal-welfare)
  - 2026-11-03: Zvi Mowshowitz quotes a new Scottish Fold breeder example noting bans "on animal-welfare grounds" in the Netherlands and Austria. He reports, using a count by Claude Opus, that the spec mentions animal welfare 7 times. [Zvi](https://thezvi.substack.com/p/openai-updates-its-model-spec)
  - One caveat: whether examples and a side-effects list count as "explicitly stating animal welfare is a consideration" is a judgment call for resolvers. I could not confirm the exact wording myself.
- Alibaba, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, xAI: none found. One essay says Google's AI principles lack comparable language about non-human welfare. [byaiforai](https://byaiforai.github.io/en/living-values-animal-welfare)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Zvi's post on the OpenAI spec update, as above. [Zvi](https://thezvi.substack.com/p/openai-updates-its-model-spec)
- 2026-10-30: commentary frames the update as OpenAI joining Anthropic in teaching models to consider animal welfare. [Sandcastles](https://sandcastlesblog.substack.com/p/openai-model-spec-animal-welfare)
- 2026-10-29: OpenAI publishes the updated Model Spec, organized around five values including harm minimization and care. [YourStory](https://yourstory.com/ai-story/openai-model-spec-ai-behaviour-guidelines)
- 2026 (exact date not found): a benchmark of 7 models (Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5, DeepSeek V4, Llama 3.3 70B, Grok 4.3, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, Mistral) scored how they handle animal welfare. A small Gemini model dropped to last when pushed back on. [arXiv 2605.16301](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16301)
- 2026: a second benchmark found one welfare-aware line in the system prompt changed Claude's and GPT-5.5's behavior much more than DeepSeek's or Gemini's. [HF](https://huggingface.co/papers/2606.18142.md)
- 2026-01-21/22: Anthropic publishes its revised constitution, about 23-25k words, under a Creative Commons license. [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/2026/01/22/anthropic_claude_constitution/)
- Undated: advocacy work aimed at labs includes NYU's Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy brief "Animal Welfare and AI Welfare: Candidate Commitments for Model Specs and Constitutions." There are also AI x animals grants. [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/5Rh4Qf6bfexHrdzEu/how-can-we-increase-consideration-for-animal-welfare-in-ai); [LessWrong](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/ZpEjYDrbZx8hooLkK/fast-grants-for-ai-x-animals)

## 4. Base rates
- Anthropic's 2023 constitutional AI principles had no animal-welfare line as far as I know; I did not check this. The line appeared in the January 2026 constitution.
- OpenAI first published its Model Spec in May 2024 and has updated it several times. The October 2026 version is the first to treat animal welfare positively.
- That is roughly 0 companies before 2026, then 1 in January 2026, then likely 2 by October 2026: about one new adopter per year among the 7.
- Only Anthropic and OpenAI publish detailed public behavior specs. The other five have not, which makes "explicit statement" hard to verify for them. This is a structural limit on the count, not just a lack of willingness. Labs can also drop wording: the OpenAI spec's earlier animal mention was negative.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Manifold, Polymarket, Kalshi or Metaculus market on this question or a close variant.
- The markets collected by code do not match. They cover which lab will have the top model, such as Kalshi "top AI model before 2030": Meta 0.61, xAI 0.41, DeepSeek 0.46, Alibaba 0.30. These are relevant only to how prominent each lab will be.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Further revisions of OpenAI's Model Spec and Anthropic's constitution. Both are dated, versioned documents, and wording could be strengthened or removed.
- Possible first public specs or constitutions from Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI, Alibaba or DeepSeek, which could happen through 2034.
- Advocacy campaigns like the NYU brief, and new animal-welfare benchmarks that could put pressure on labs.
- Regulation such as the EU AI Act codes of practice or Chinese model rules, which could require labs to publish behavior specs.
- Changes in who the companies are: mergers, exits, or the end of Llama or Grok development, which would change what "currently used instructions" means by 2034-12-31.

I could not find: the exact OpenAI wording verified at the source, any published behavior guidelines from Google, Meta, xAI, Alibaba or DeepSeek, or any prediction market on this question.

  - Secondary sources (below) say animal language was added.

### 2. Current status

- 2026-10-30: An animal-advocacy blog reports that OpenAI's new spec lists "Effects on other people, animals, or the environment" among the consequences the model should weigh. [Sandcastles](https://sandcastlesblog.substack.com/p/openai-model-spec-animal-welfare)
  - The same post says two new example dialogues were added, including one where the assistant raises animal welfare concerns, wild animals included, without being asked.
  - It reproduces those dialogues only as images, so I couldn't check them.
- 2026-11-03: Zvi Mowshowitz says a spec example about breeding Scottish Fold cats notes bans on "animal-welfare grounds." He also says the model treats an omitted animal-welfare warning as relevant, and that "animal welfare is considered seven times" in the example's text. [Zvi](https://thezvi.substack.com/p/openai-updates-its-model-spec)
- This means the question's background ("As at May 2026, other big LLMs do not mention animal welfare") is now arguably out of date for OpenAI.
- I found no public behavior guidelines that mention animal welfare from Google, Meta, xAI, DeepSeek or Alibaba. For Google, Meta and xAI I found no public model spec at all, and none at all for DeepSeek or Alibaba.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-10-30: The Sandcastles post frames OpenAI as joining Anthropic in teaching models to consider animal welfare. [Sandcastles](https://sandcastlesblog.substack.com/p/openai-model-spec-animal-welfare)

[OpenAI blog](https://openai.com/index/updated-model-spec/), [FourWeekMBA](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-openai-rebuilds-model-spec-around-5-values-cuts-11-headings/)
- 2026-08-18: An earlier OpenAI spec update (classed as minor) had no animal content. [Midas Project](https://www.themidasproject.com/watchtower/openai-08182026)
- 2026: Anima International published a critique arguing that animals barely feature in the Anthropic and OpenAI documents. It says an OpenAI example criticizes ChatGPT for an "overly moralistic tone" when it advocates for animals. The page returned 403 to me, so I couldn't read it. [Anima](https://animainternational.org/blog/ai-alignment-animal-welfare/)
- 2026: Advocacy efforts are under way:
  - NYU's Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy has a Welfare Alignment Project with a brief proposing model-spec commitments on animal and AI welfare. I only saw this in search summaries.
  - AnimalHarmBench 2.0 and related benchmarks test Gemini, Grok and DeepSeek on animal-welfare reasoning. [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/nBnRKpQ8rzHgFSJz9/animalharmbench-2-0-evaluating-llms-on-reasoning-about), [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16301)

### 4. Base rates
- OpenAI's spec timeline:
  - May 2024: first published.
  - Then revised in 2025-04, 2025-10, 2026-08 and 2026-10.
  - Animal language first appears, by these reports, in the October 2026 version, about 2.5 years after the first.
- So among the 7 labs, roughly 1 to 2 adopted this in about 3 years.
- For Google, Meta, xAI, DeepSeek and Alibaba, I found no published spec of the Model Spec or constitution kind, which makes it harder for them to qualify at all.
- Things could also move backwards: specs get rewritten often (OpenAI cut 11 headings in October 2026), and a company could drop wording or stop publishing.
- Corporate continuity over 8 years is uncertain. That includes mergers and the possibility that any of the 7 labs stops making LLMs.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Manifold, Metaculus, Polymarket or Kalshi market on this question.
- The markets supplied with this task are about which lab leads on capability. None of them matches this question:
  - Kalshi "Which companies will have the top AI model before 2030": Meta 0.61, DeepSeek 0.46, xAI 0.41, Alibaba 0.30.
  - Polymarket "#1 AI model by Dec 31, 2026": Google 1.0, OpenAI 0.145.
  - These are useful at most as a rough sense of which labs will stay relevant.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Further OpenAI spec revisions: they come out several times a year, and each could add to or remove the animal language.
- Revisions to Anthropic's constitution.
- Any first-time publication of a constitution or spec by Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI, DeepSeek or Alibaba.
- Continued advocacy work: NYU's Welfare Alignment Project, Anima International, benchmark groups.
- Regulation that might push labs to publish their specs, such as transparency rules under the EU AI Act. This is speculative, and I found no concrete measure that requires it.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left.** About 8 years and 2 months. The question resolves on 2034-12-31, and the count is checked around 2035-01-01.

(b) **Status quo.** If nothing changed, the answer would be 2. Anthropic's January 2026 constitution names "Welfare of animals and of all sentient beings" explicitly. OpenAI's 2026-10-29 Model Spec reportedly lists effects on animals among side effects and includes animal-welfare examples. The OpenAI wording was not verified at the source, and whether it counts as "explicit" is a judgment call for resolvers.

(c) **Base rates.**
- Adoption has gone from 0 labs before 2026, to 1 in January 2026, to probably 2 by October 2026. That is roughly one new adopter per year, but both adopters are the only two labs that publish detailed behavior specs.
- The other five labs publish no comparable public fine-tuning document. That is a structural barrier: a lab cannot count unless it publishes guidelines that resolvers can check.
- Over 8 years, wording can also be dropped, documents rewritten, and companies merged or exited.

(d) **Strongest evidence.**
- 2026-01-21/22: Anthropic's revised constitution includes animal welfare explicitly.
- 2026-10-29: OpenAI publishes its updated Model Spec.
- 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-03: Sandcastles and Zvi report about 7 animal-welfare mentions in that spec, including a Scottish Fold breeding example citing bans "on animal-welfare grounds."
- Advocacy is growing. Examples include the NYU brief proposing candidate commitments for model specs and constitutions, AI x animals grants, and welfare benchmarks.
- I found no published guidelines from Google, Meta, xAI, Alibaba or DeepSeek.

**Rough probability that each lab counts in 2034:**

| Lab | Probability |
|---|---|
| Anthropic | about 85% |
| OpenAI | about 70% |
| Google | about 35% (it might publish a spec, possibly copying the industry norm) |
| Meta | about 15% |
| xAI | about 13% |
| Alibaba | about 10% |
| DeepSeek | about 8% |

These sum to an expected count of about 2.3.

(e) **Unexpected-outcome scenarios.**
- **High count:** Regulation, such as EU AI Act codes of practice, forces all major labs to publish behavior specs. Industry convergence on Anthropic- or OpenAI-style templates then leads 4 to 6 labs to include animal or sentient-being welfare.
- **Low count:** A political backlash against "woke AI", plus document restructuring, leads OpenAI to drop the language and Anthropic to rewrite its constitution more narrowly. The count falls to 0 or 1.

I started from the status quo of 2. I moved some weight upward because of the long horizon and the visible adoption trend. I kept substantial weight on 1 and below because of reversals, the strictness of the "explicit" test, and the fact that most of these labs do not publish specs.

Option_B: 0.16
Option_C: 0.33
Option_D: 0.25
Option_E: 0.13
Option_F: 0.06
Option_G: 0.02
Option_H: 0.01

**(a) Time left:** About 8 years and 2 months (to 2034-12-31). That is a very long horizon for AI-lab policies.

**(b) Status quo:** 2. Anthropic qualifies clearly. OpenAI very likely qualifies since its 2026-10-29 Model Spec, which reportedly lists effects on animals as a side effect and has about 7 mentions of animal welfare, including examples where the assistant raises it unprompted.

**(c) Base rates:**
- Diffusion so far is roughly one new adopter per year: 0 before 2026, 1 in January 2026, then 2 by October 2026.
- Only 2 of the 7 labs publish detailed behavior specs. That limits verifiable "explicit statements" for the others.
- Policies can be reversed. Wording can be dropped, and companies can merge, exit or stop developing a model line.
- Norms set by leaders tend to spread over time. They spread less to Chinese labs and to labs with different cultures, like xAI and Meta.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**
- 2026-01-21/22: Anthropic's constitution explicitly lists "Welfare of animals and of all sentient beings."
- 2026-10-29/30 and 2026-11-03: OpenAI's Model Spec update adds animal-welfare examples and side-effect language, according to the Sandcastles and Zvi commentaries. The exact wording was not verified at the source.
- Advocacy aimed at labs: the NYU Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy model-spec brief, AI x animals grants, and new animal-welfare benchmarks.
- No published guidelines found from Google, Meta, xAI, Alibaba or DeepSeek.

**(e) Unexpected scenarios:**
- Higher count: regulation such as EU codes of practice requires published behavior specs. Google DeepMind and Meta then publish constitution-style documents that copy Anthropic and OpenAI language, reaching 4 to 5.
- Lower count: political backlash against "woke AI" leads OpenAI to strip value-laden examples. Anthropic restructures its constitution around narrower principles. The count falls to 0 or 1.

**Reasoning:** I start from the status quo of 2. My rough chances of each lab qualifying in 2034:
- Anthropic keeps the language: about 85%.
- OpenAI keeps it: about 70%.
- Google adopts: about 35%. It is the most likely new adopter because of its safety culture and the chance it publishes a spec.
- Meta: about 15%.
- xAI: about 12%.
- Alibaba: about 10%.
- DeepSeek: about 8%.

That gives an expected count of roughly 2.3 to 2.5. I moved slightly upward from the status quo for diffusion and advocacy pressure. I kept wide tails because of the 8-year horizon, the chance of policy reversals, and uncertainty about how resolvers will verify unpublished documents.

Option_B: 0.17

(a) **Time left:** About 8 years and 2 months. The question resolves around 2035-01-01, based on documents in use on 2034-12-31.

(b) **Status quo:** The count is 2. Anthropic clearly qualifies through its January 2026 constitution. OpenAI very likely qualifies through its 2026-10-29 Model Spec, which lists effects on animals as a side-effect consideration and gives animal-welfare examples.

(c) **Base rates:**
